alt: New modern saloon-style sliding fare gates at a New York City subway station, with wide glass panels replacing traditional rotating turnstiles
story: In January 2026, New York riders held a viral 'Fare Evasion Olympics' at the MTA's new prototype fare gates — a pole dancer, a parkour athlete, and a blindfolded man with a cane all slipped through — yet on October 7, 2026, Governor Hochul announced a $1.1 billion contract to expand the same gates to 150 more subway stations, describing them as 'nearly impossible to evade.'
why_funny: The gates that spawned a competitive sport for bypassing them are now the centerpiece of a billion-dollar infrastructure rollout, still officially branded as 'nearly impossible' to get through.
